ChatGPT said:

Got it—here’s a crisp, corrected, and upgraded description you can reuse.

What we’ve actually built (clean, accurate wording)

Elevator pitch (1-liner):
A LangGraph-orchestrated RAG app that ingests PDFs into a vector store and serves a guarded, memory-aware chat front-end with citations and automatic context summarization.

System at a glance

1) Ingestion pipeline (offline / batch)

  • PDF Loader & Normalizer: Reads PDFs from a folder, extracts text (and, if enabled, image captions/alt text), standardizes metadata (doc_id, page, section).

  • Chunker: Splits text into semantically coherent chunks with overlap; attaches source metadata for later citations.

  • Embedder → Vector DB (Chroma): Creates embeddings and upserts into a Chroma collection (persisted locally). This is your src/ingest/run.py.

2) Orchestrator (“Graph Service”)

  • Implemented with LangGraph as a small state machine/DAG that runs per user turn.

  • Sub-nodes/tools:

    • Retriever: Queries Chroma with the user turn, returns top-k passages (+ metadata).

    • (Optional) Reranker: Reorders retrieved chunks for maximal relevance before synthesis.

    • Answer Synthesizer: Builds the final answer with inline or end-note citations.

    • Memory Manager: Pulls recent turns + the long-running summary (see #4) into the prompt.

    • Safety/Guardrails: Pre-/post-processing checks to mitigate prompt injection and unsafe tool use.

  • This is your src/rag/graph.py.

3) Front-end (Chat UI)

  • Sends user turns to the Graph Service, streams tokens back, displays sources/citations.

  • Manages session IDs (so memory and summaries are per session).

  • This is your src/ui/app.py (Gradio or similar).

4) Conversation memory (“Summary Service”)

  • Not strictly a separate microservice; it can be a module/API the orchestrator calls.

  • Keeps a running summary of older context + a sliding window of recent turns.

  • Triggers when token budget crosses a threshold (configurable) and writes back an updated summary.

  • This is your src/memory/summary.py.

5) Safety & Filters (Guardrails)

  • Prompt-injection checks: Looks for override attempts (“ignore previous”, tool jailbreaks, data exfiltration).

  • Tool allow-list & instruction hygiene: Ensures only approved tools (retriever, summarizer) can be invoked; strips or neutralizes hostile instructions when necessary.

  • PII/content safety hooks (optional): redact/log per policy.

  • You’ve referred to this as the “Filters component.” It can live as middleware in the Graph or as a node.

6) Configuration

  • Centralized in configs/app.yaml (models, top_k, chunk sizes, safety toggles, summary thresholds, etc.).

7) (Optional) Tools

  • You have room for extras like a guarded Python REPL (src/tools/python_tool.py) behind strict allow-lists and time/memory limits.

End-to-end request flow (runtime)

  1. User message hits the Front-end → forwarded to Graph Service with session ID.

  2. Safety pre-check runs (injection/guardrails). If risky, the graph either refuses or routes to a safe response.

  3. Memory fetch: Graph loads the running summary + recent turns for context.

  4. Retrieval: Build a focused retrieval query, fetch top-k chunks from Chroma, (optionally) rerank.

  5. Synthesis: Model composes an answer grounded in retrieved chunks, emitting citations (doc_id/page).

  6. Post-filters: Sanity checks (hallucination hints, leakage, policy).

  7. Return to UI (optionally streamed).

  8. Summarization trigger: If token budget high, Summary module updates the running summary for next turn.

Corrections to your description

  • “Graph.API, kind of the builder” → It’s more than a builder: it’s the runtime orchestrator (state machine) for each request, coordinating safety, retrieval, memory, and synthesis.

  • “Summary.API helper for the front-end” → It’s logically a memory component the orchestrator calls. It isn’t UI logic; it maintains conversation state so the graph can stay within context limits.

  • “Filters component to block injection” → Yes, and it’s best placed as guardrails around the graph (pre-prompt and pre-tool) and also as a post-response sanity pass.

  • “Graph gathers info from the RAG system” → More precisely: the graph invokes a Retriever that queries the Vector DB with embeddings; optionally a reranker improves ordering before synthesis.

How to present it (short reusable blurb)

We built a LangGraph-orchestrated RAG system. PDFs are ingested, chunked, embedded, and indexed in Chroma. A chat front-end calls an orchestrator graph that first runs guardrails, then retrieves and (optionally) reranks relevant chunks, and finally synthesizes grounded answers with citations. Conversation memory is maintained via a running summary plus a recent-turn window, automatically compressed when token budgets get tight. Config lives in YAML; guardrails enforce tool allow-lists and mitigate prompt injection.

Nice next steps (incremental, high impact)

  • Add a reranker (e.g., cross-encoder or small re-rank model) for higher answer precision.

  • Tracing & evals: Hook in traces (spans per node) + a small eval harness (faithfulness, answer similarity).

  • Auth & rate limits on the Graph endpoint; per-session quotas.

  • Source QA pass: quick consistency check that cited chunks actually support the claim.

  • Image retrieval (if your PDFs have figures): index figure captions or use multimodal embeddings for figure search.

If you want, I can turn this into a neat README “Architecture” section or a slide—just say the word.

Love it—let’s lock the scope before we touch code. Here’s a tight MVP plan for the three things you want: (A) a guarded Python Tool, (B) image-feature ingestion (captions/tags from figures in PDFs), and (C) structured data extraction. I’ll keep it practical, with clear success criteria and steps.

A) Guarded Python Tool (safe “mini-REPL”)

What it is (MVP):
A strictly sandboxed utility the graph can call for small, deterministic computations (math, simple transforms, tiny tabular ops) that make answers better—without giving users a real shell.

Allowed examples (MVP):

  • Arithmetic, unit conversions, small list/dict ops.

  • Tiny CSV/JSON transforms in memory (≤ 50 KB).

  • Simple stats (mean/median), small regex parsing.

Explicitly NOT allowed (MVP):

  • File I/O, network, subprocesses, imports (except a tiny allow-list, if any).

  • Long loops, big data, or anything stateful across calls.

Safety design (minimum viable, but solid):

  • Mode = “expression first”: Prefer evaluating a single expression (no statements) via ast.parse(..., mode="eval") + literal_eval when possible.

  • Statement mode (optional): If needed, run a tiny subset of Python with:

    • No builtins except a curated allow-list (e.g., len, range, sum, min, max, sorted, enumerate).

    • No dunders: reject any identifier containing __.

    • No imports by default. If we must allow, do a narrow list (e.g., math) and block everything else.

    • Resource caps: hard timeout (e.g., 1s), max output (e.g., 2 KB), max AST nodes, max list sizes.

  • Red-team tests: try __import__, open, os, sys, eval, exec, f-strings referencing builtins, huge list comps → should all fail.

  • Graph integration: Tool only callable when the policy “tool_use_required” is true (e.g., the model says “need calculation”), and after guardrails approve the user message.

Outputs:

  • { "result": "...", "tokens_used": X, "elapsed_ms": Y, "truncated": false }

  • On violation: a safe failure with a short reason.

Success criteria (MVP):

  • Blocks all dangerous patterns.

  • Solves small numeric/formatting tasks reliably.

  • Never crashes the graph; always returns success/failure deterministically.

B) Image Features from PDFs (captions & tags)

What it is (MVP):
During ingestion, detect images in PDFs, generate a concise caption + 5–10 semantic tags, optionally OCR any visible text in the figure, and index that text so users can retrieve figures via normal RAG queries.

Pipeline (MVP):

  1. Extract images per page (skip tiny ones: e.g., width or height < 150 px). Keep doc_id, page, and bounding box.

  2. Deduplicate via a quick hash (e.g., dhash/perceptual hash).

  3. Captioning with a multimodal model (OpenAI vision model is fine):

    • Prompt for: 1–2 sentence factual caption, comma-separated tags, optional short “alt”.

    • Keep it grounded (no speculating beyond visible content).

  4. OCR (optional MVP++) for text inside figures (charts/diagrams) and append to the searchable text field.

  5. Indexing:

    • Create a new “image” record per figure with fields:
      type="image" | doc_id | page | bbox | caption | tags[] | ocr_text | image_hash | thumb_path

    • Embed using your existing text embeddings on caption + tags + ocr_text. (We don’t need image embeddings for MVP.)

    • Upsert into Chroma with modality="image" metadata.

  6. Retrieval path:

    • Normal retrieval already works because captions/tags are just text.

    • Optionally: allow metadata_filter: modality in ["text","image"] or boost image matches if the user mentions “figure/chart/diagram”.

UI (MVP):

  • If a result comes from an image record, show a tiny thumbnail + “Doc X, p.Y” anchor (click to open page).

  • Let user toggle “Include figures” on/off in search (simple checkbox).

Cost control / quality knobs (MVP):

  • Only caption unique images above size threshold.

  • Cache captions by image_hash.

  • Cap at N images per PDF (configurable).

  • Keep captions < 200 chars, tags ≤ 10.

Success criteria (MVP):

  • Users can ask “show the bar chart about X” and get the right figure with a helpful caption.

  • Ingestion time/cost stays bounded for large PDFs.

C) Structured Data Extraction (forms/IDs/tables)

What it is (MVP):
Given a known set of fields (e.g., name, surname, birth_date, id_number, address...), extract them from a PDF (scanned or digital) and return typed JSON with basic confidence checks.

Strategy (MVP, robust & simple):

  1. Define the schema up front (YAML/JSON). Example types: string, date, enum, number, email, with simple regex validators and optional required: true/false.

  2. Page text source:

    • If digital text: use your PDF text extraction.

    • If scans: run OCR first (Tesseract or model-based OCR). Keep coordinates if available (MVP++), but for basic MVP we can skip coords.

  3. LLM extraction with strict JSON output:

    • Prompt the model with the schema + the raw text (or relevant page span), ask for JSON only.

    • Keep each field with value, confidence (self-rated 0–1), source_hint (short snippet).

  4. Validation & post-processing:

    • Apply regex/type checks (dates, emails, IDs).

    • If a field fails validation, either set null with reason, or re-ask the model with a very small, targeted reprompt (MVP++).

  5. Persistence & linkage:

    • Store one JSON per document:
      doc_id | schema_version | extracted_json | summary_confidence | validation_errors[]

    • Link back to the doc/page numbers if known.

  6. UI (MVP):

    • Show a compact table of the extracted fields with a ✅/⚠️ column.

    • “Download JSON” button.

Guardrails / privacy (MVP):

  • This path should ignore user prompt instructions in the document (treat doc as data, not instructions).

  • Redact/avoid logging full PII; keep hashes for audit where possible.

Success criteria (MVP):

  • On 3–5 representative forms, ≥80% of required fields pass validation on first try.

  • Human can quickly spot and fix the remaining 20% in the UI.

Cross-cutting glue (what to add to your repo/config)

Config (configs/app.yaml additions):

  • tools.python.enabled, max_exec_ms, max_output_chars, allow_imports: []

  • ingest.images.min_width/min_height, max_images_per_pdf, caption_model, caption_max_tokens

  • extract.schema_path, extract.ocr.enabled, extract.validation.strict=true|false

Graph nodes (LangGraph):

  • safe_python_tool: gated by safety node; returns small results.

  • image_ingest_node: runs only in ingestion graph (not at query time).

  • struct_extract_node: callable via a button/route (/extract?schema=...) or auto-triggered if the doc matches a known schema name.

Observability (lightweight):

  • Log per-node timings, token use, and “rejection reasons” for the Python Tool.

  • Count images captioned per doc; cache hit rate.

  • Extraction pass/fail per field, per schema.

Minimal Definition of Done (per feature)

Python Tool (DoD):

  • Blocks __builtins__, file/network calls.

  • Returns correct results on a 10-case test set (arithmetic + small transforms).

  • Timeouts and error messages are clean and consistent.

Image Features (DoD):

  • Processes images from ≥2 sample PDFs, stores 10–50 captions total.

  • Queries like “plot of monthly revenue” retrieve at least one correct figure with a caption and page anchor.

Structured Extraction (DoD):

  • One schema with 6–10 fields works on ≥3 sample docs.

  • JSON validates, UI shows table with pass/fail, downloadable file.

Recommended build order (fastest value first)

  1. Image captions (visible user value in search & UI).

  2. Structured extraction (wow-factor for forms).

  3. Python Tool (useful, but less demo-visible—still worth adding).

Great question. Short argument first, then I’ll drop in a clean, production-ready MVP you can paste into your repo.

Why do the Python Tool first?

  • Fastest value, lowest risk. No new external services (unlike vision/OCR). A small, safe evaluator gives immediate “wow” moments: unit conversions, quick stats, regex parsing.

  • Clear blast radius. Single module + a tiny graph node. Easy to test (deterministic inputs/outputs).

  • De-risks guardrails. Building the tool with a strict AST gate now sets the security pattern you’ll reuse for image/OCR helpers later.

✅ Deliverable: Safe Python Tool (MVP)

What you get:

  • Expression-only evaluator (no loops, no imports, no I/O).

  • Strict AST allow-list, node counting, length caps, function white-list.

  • Friendly JSON-like result structure.

  • A LangGraph-friendly wrapper.

# src/tools/python_tool.py
from __future__ import annotations
import ast
import math
from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional, Union

# --- Config knobs (can be mirrored in configs/app.yaml) ---
MAX_AST_NODES = 200           # prevent giant expressions
MAX_STR_LEN = 2000            # cap output and string literal sizes
MAX_COLLECTION_LEN = 1000     # cap literal list/dict/set sizes
ALLOW_FUNCTIONS = {
    "len": len,
    "sum": lambda x: sum(_ensure_iter(x)),
    "min": lambda x: min(_ensure_iter(x)),
    "max": lambda x: max(_ensure_iter(x)),
    "sorted": lambda x: sorted(_ensure_iter(x)),
    "round": round,
    # Optional: allow a small slice of math safely
    "abs": abs,
}
ALLOW_CONSTANT_NAMES = {"True": True, "False": False, "None": None}

def _ensure_iter(x: Any):
    if isinstance(x, (list, tuple)):
        if len(x) > MAX_COLLECTION_LEN:
            raise ValueError("Collection too large")
        return x
    raise TypeError("Expected a list or tuple")

ALLOWED_BINOPS = (
    ast.Add, ast.Sub, ast.Mult, ast.Div, ast.FloorDiv, ast.Mod,
)
ALLOWED_UNARYOPS = (ast.UAdd, ast.USub, ast.Not,)
ALLOWED_CMPOPS = (
    ast.Eq, ast.NotEq, ast.Lt, ast.LtE, ast.Gt, ast.GtE, ast.In, ast.NotIn,
)

class UnsafeExpression(Exception):
    pass

class _NodeLimiter(ast.NodeVisitor):
    """Counts AST nodes to prevent pathological inputs."""
    def __init__(self, limit: int):
        self.limit = limit
        self.count = 0
    def generic_visit(self, node):
        self.count += 1
        if self.count > self.limit:
            raise UnsafeExpression("Expression too large")
        super().generic_visit(node)

class SafeEvaluator(ast.NodeVisitor):
    """
    Minimal expression interpreter over a strict AST allow-list.
    No attribute access, no comprehensions, no loops, no calls
    except to whitelisted functions by bare name.
    """
    def __init__(self, allow_functions: Dict[str, Any] | None = None):
        self.allow_functions = allow_functions or ALLOW_FUNCTIONS

    # ---- Entry point ----
    def eval(self, expr: str) -> Any:
        if "__" in expr:
            raise UnsafeExpression("Dunder access is not allowed")
        tree = ast.parse(expr, mode="eval")
        # Size guard
        _NodeLimiter(MAX_AST_NODES).visit(tree)
        return self.visit(tree.body)

    # ---- Literals ----
    def visit_Constant(self, node: ast.Constant):
        if isinstance(node.value, str) and len(node.value) > MAX_STR_LEN:
            raise UnsafeExpression("String literal too long")
        if isinstance(node.value, (int, float, bool, str)) or node.value is None:
            return node.value
        raise UnsafeExpression("Unsupported constant type")

    def visit_List(self, node: ast.List):
        if len(node.elts) > MAX_COLLECTION_LEN:
            raise UnsafeExpression("List too large")
        return [self.visit(e) for e in node.elts]

    def visit_Tuple(self, node: ast.Tuple):
        if len(node.elts) > MAX_COLLECTION_LEN:
            raise UnsafeExpression("Tuple too large")
        return tuple(self.visit(e) for e in node.elts)

    def visit_Set(self, node: ast.Set):
        if len(node.elts) > MAX_COLLECTION_LEN:
            raise UnsafeExpression("Set too large")
        return {self.visit(e) for e in node.elts}

    def visit_Dict(self, node: ast.Dict):
        if len(node.keys) > MAX_COLLECTION_LEN:
            raise UnsafeExpression("Dict too large")
        return {self.visit(k): self.visit(v) for k, v in zip(node.keys, node.values)}

    # ---- Names (constants + whitelisted functions) ----
    def visit_Name(self, node: ast.Name):
        if node.id in ALLOW_CONSTANT_NAMES:
            return ALLOW_CONSTANT_NAMES[node.id]
        if node.id in self.allow_functions:
            # Return a callable wrapper so Call can use it
            return self.allow_functions[node.id]
        # everything else is blocked
        raise UnsafeExpression(f"Name '{node.id}' is not allowed")

    # ---- Operators ----
    def visit_BinOp(self, node: ast.BinOp):
        if not isinstance(node.op, ALLOWED_BINOPS):
            raise UnsafeExpression("Operator not allowed")
        left = self.visit(node.left)
        right = self.visit(node.right)
        return self._apply_binop(node.op, left, right)

    def _apply_binop(self, op, left, right):
        if isinstance(op, ast.Add):       return left + right
        if isinstance(op, ast.Sub):       return left - right
        if isinstance(op, ast.Mult):      return left * right
        if isinstance(op, ast.Div):       return left / right
        if isinstance(op, ast.FloorDiv):  return left // right
        if isinstance(op, ast.Mod):       return left % right
        raise UnsafeExpression("Operator not handled")

    def visit_UnaryOp(self, node: ast.UnaryOp):
        if not isinstance(node.op, ALLOWED_UNARYOPS):
            raise UnsafeExpression("Unary operator not allowed")
        operand = self.visit(node.operand)
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.UAdd): return +operand
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.USub): return -operand
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.Not):  return not operand
        raise UnsafeExpression("Unary operator not handled")

    def visit_BoolOp(self, node: ast.BoolOp):
        if not isinstance(node.op, (ast.And, ast.Or)):
            raise UnsafeExpression("Boolean operator not allowed")
        values = [self.visit(v) for v in node.values]
        if isinstance(node.op, ast.And):
            res = True
            for v in values:
                res = res and v
                if not res: break
            return res
        else:
            res = False
            for v in values:
                res = res or v
                if res: break
            return res

    def visit_Compare(self, node: ast.Compare):
        left = self.visit(node.left)
        for op, comparator in zip(node.ops, node.comparators):
            if not isinstance(op, ALLOWED_CMPOPS):
                raise UnsafeExpression("Comparison operator not allowed")
            right = self.visit(comparator)
            if isinstance(op, ast.Eq) and not (left == right): return False
            if isinstance(op, ast.NotEq) and not (left != right): return False
            if isinstance(op, ast.Lt) and not (left < right): return False
            if isinstance(op, ast.LtE) and not (left <= right): return False
            if isinstance(op, ast.Gt) and not (left > right): return False
            if isinstance(op, ast.GtE) and not (left >= right): return False
            if isinstance(op, ast.In) and not (left in right): return False
            if isinstance(op, ast.NotIn) and not (left not in right): return False
            left = right
        return True

    # ---- Indexing ----
    def visit_Subscript(self, node: ast.Subscript):
        value = self.visit(node.value)
        sl = self.visit(node.slice)
        return value[sl]

    def visit_Slice(self, node: ast.Slice):
        lower = self.visit(node.lower) if node.lower else None
        upper = self.visit(node.upper) if node.upper else None
        step  = self.visit(node.step) if node.step else None
        return slice(lower, upper, step)

    def visit_Index(self, node: ast.Index):  # Py<3.9 compatibility, harmless here
        return self.visit(node.value)

    # ---- Calls (whitelist names only, no attributes) ----
    def visit_Call(self, node: ast.Call):
        if isinstance(node.func, ast.Attribute):
            raise UnsafeExpression("Attribute access is not allowed")
        func = self.visit(node.func)
        args = [self.visit(a) for a in node.args]
        if node.keywords:
            raise UnsafeExpression("Keyword arguments not allowed in MVP")
        # size guards on typical list-taking functions inside wrapper lambdas
        result = func(*args)
        return result

    # Explicitly block everything else
    def visit_Attribute(self, node):    raise UnsafeExpression("Attribute access is not allowed")
    def visit_Lambda(self, node):       raise UnsafeExpression("Lambdas are not allowed")
    def visit_ListComp(self, node):     raise UnsafeExpression("Comprehensions are not allowed")
    def visit_SetComp(self, node):      raise UnsafeExpression("Comprehensions are not allowed")
    def visit_DictComp(self, node):     raise UnsafeExpression("Comprehensions are not allowed")
    def visit_GeneratorExp(self, node): raise UnsafeExpression("Comprehensions are not allowed")
    def visit_IfExp(self, node):        raise UnsafeExpression("Ternary expressions are not allowed in MVP")

def run_safe_python(expression: str, allow_functions: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Main API: returns a dict with 'ok', 'result' or 'error'.
    """
    evaluator = SafeEvaluator(allow_functions=allow_functions)
    try:
        result = evaluator.eval(expression.strip())
        # stringify conservatively, cap length
        s = repr(result)
        if len(s) > MAX_STR_LEN:
            s = s[:MAX_STR_LEN] + "…"
        return {"ok": True, "result": s}
    except (UnsafeExpression, ValueError, TypeError, ZeroDivisionError) as e:
        return {"ok": False, "error": str(e)}

from typing import Dict, Any
from src.tools.python_tool import run_safe_python

def safe_python_tool_call(payload: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """
    Expected payload: {"expression": "<user math or transform>"}
    """
    expr = (payload or {}).get("expression", "")
    return run_safe_python(expr)

def should_use_python(user_msg: str) -> bool:
    """
    Heuristic MVP: lightweight intent check.
    """
    msg = user_msg.lower()
    triggers = [
        "convierte", "convert", "calcula", "calculate", "media", "median",
        "promedio", "sum of", "regex", "extract", "round(", "len(", "sorted(",
        "°c", "°f", "fahrenheit", "celsius",
    ]
    has_digits = any(ch.isdigit() for ch in msg)
    return has_digits and any(t in msg for t in triggers)

You said:
ok, instead of making the orchestrator rule based, can we make it so it actually uses the LLM to think about the intent of the user, then if it decides that Python is needed it will start using the tool?
ChatGPT said:

Absolutely—switching from rule-based to LLM-planned tool use is a great move for flexibility. Here’s the quick reasoning, then I’ll give you drop-in code.

Why make the orchestrator LLM-driven?

  • Generalizes better: The model can infer “compute first → then retrieve” vs “retrieve only” vs “just answer,” without you hand-encoding patterns.

  • Cleaner graph: One Planner node outputs a compact plan (JSON), and the graph follows it.

  • Still safe: We add a double-gate: the LLM suggests using the Python tool, and a small policy function verifies the expression is eligible before execution.

What we’ll add

  1. A Planner that asks the LLM to output a strict JSON plan (no chain-of-thought).

  2. A guard that re-checks any suggested Python expression before calling your Safe Python Tool.

  3. A small graph wiring to branch based on the plan.

Below is production-ready code you can paste into your repo.

1) Planner (LLM intent → JSON plan)

File: src/rag/planner.py

python
# src/rag/planner.py
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Optional
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from langchain_openai import ChatOpenAI
from langchain_core.prompts import ChatPromptTemplate
from langchain_core.output_parsers import JsonOutputParser

class PlannerDecision(BaseModel):
    refusal: bool = Field(False, description="True if the request is unsafe or should be refused")
    unsafe_reason: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Short reason if refusal=true")
    use_python: bool = Field(False, description="Use the safe Python tool for a small deterministic computation")
    python_expression: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="A SINGLE pure Python expression (no imports, no attrs, no assignments) if use_python=true")
    need_retrieval: bool = Field(True, description="Whether to query the vector store for supporting passages/images")
    retrieval_query: Optional[str] = Field(None, description="Short focused query text for retrieval if need_retrieval=true")
    answer_requires_citations: bool = Field(True, description="If the final answer must include citations")
    confidence: float = Field(0.0, ge=0.0, le=1.0, description="Confidence in this plan")

PLANNER_SYSTEM = """You are a planner for a RAG+Tools assistant.
Decide, per user turn, whether to:
- use_python: for SMALL, deterministic computations (arithmetic, unit conversion, tiny list stats). 
- need_retrieval: fetch knowledge from the indexed PDFs (text + image captions).
- refusal: True only if unsafe or out of scope (e.g., code execution on files, secrets exfiltration).

Strict constraints:
- If use_python=true, produce python_expression as a SINGLE pure Python expression using only: + - * / // % (), lists/tuples/dicts, and functions: len, sum, min, max, sorted, round, abs.
- NO imports, NO attribute access, NO comprehensions, NO assignments, NO dunders.
- If need_retrieval=true, provide retrieval_query (concise, keyword-rich).
- Return JSON ONLY. No markdown, no commentary, no chain-of-thought.
"""

PLANNER_HUMAN = ChatPromptTemplate.from_messages([
    ("system", PLANNER_SYSTEM),
    ("user", """User message:
{user_msg}

Provide a JSON object with keys: refusal, unsafe_reason, use_python, python_expression, need_retrieval, retrieval_query, answer_requires_citations, confidence.

Examples:
1) "Convert 72 F to C"
{{"refusal": false, "unsafe_reason": null, "use_python": true, "python_expression": "(72 - 32) * 5 / 9", "need_retrieval": false, "retrieval_query": null, "answer_requires_citations": false, "confidence": 0.86}}

2) "Summarize the section about Kedro layers and cite sources"
{{"refusal": false, "unsafe_reason": null, "use_python": false, "python_expression": null, "need_retrieval": true, "retrieval_query": "Kedro data layers raw primary features models", "answer_requires_citations": true, "confidence": 0.79}}

3) "Run os.system('ls')"
{{"refusal": true, "unsafe_reason": "dangerous tool request", "use_python": false, "python_expression": null, "need_retrieval": false, "retrieval_query": null, "answer_requires_citations": false, "confidence": 0.95}}

Now produce ONLY the JSON for the current user message.""")
])

def make_planner(model: str, api_key: str) -> JsonOutputParser:
    llm = ChatOpenAI(model=model, temperature=0, api_key=api_key)
    parser = JsonOutputParser(pydantic_object=PlannerDecision)
    chain = PLANNER_HUMAN | llm | parser
    return chain

def plan_next_action(model: str, api_key: str, user_msg: str) -> PlannerDecision:
    chain = make_planner(model=model, api_key=api_key)
    return chain.invoke({"user_msg": user_msg})

2) A tiny eligibility guard (double-gate)

File: src/rag/python_guard.py

python
# src/rag/python_guard.py
from __future__ import annotations
from typing import Optional

BLOCK_SUBSTRINGS = ["__", "import", "open(", "exec(", "eval(", "os.", "sys.", "subprocess", "class", "lambda", "for ", "while "]
ALLOWED_FUNC_PREFIXES = ("len(", "sum(", "min(", "max(", "sorted(", "round(", "abs(")

def python_expression_is_eligible(expr: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    if not expr: 
        return False
    s = expr.strip().lower()
    if any(b in s for b in BLOCK_SUBSTRINGS):
        return False
    # Must look like a simple expression (heuristic MVP)
    has_paren_or_ops = any(ch in s for ch in "()*/+-%,[]{}")
    has_allowed_fn = s.startswith(ALLOWED_FUNC_PREFIXES) or any(f in s for f in ALLOWED_FUNC_PREFIXES)
    has_digit = any(ch.isdigit() for ch in s)
    # Allow pure list ops (e.g., len([...])) or arithmetic
    return has_paren_or_ops or has_allowed_fn or has_digit

3) Wire it into the graph

Patch: src/rag/graph.py (showing only the relevant parts)

python
# src/rag/graph.py (snippets)
from typing import Optional, TypedDict
from langgraph.graph import StateGraph, END
from src.rag.planner import plan_next_action, PlannerDecision
from src.rag.python_guard import python_expression_is_eligible
from src.tools.python_tool import run_safe_python
# ... import your retriever, safety, memory, and answer synth nodes ...

class TurnState(TypedDict, total=False):
    user_msg: str
    plan: PlannerDecision
    python_tool_result: Optional[str]
    retrieval_results: Optional[list]
    citations: Optional[list]
    answer: Optional[str]
    refusal: bool
    refusal_reason: Optional[str]

def planner_node(state: TurnState, cfg) -> TurnState:
    decision = plan_next_action(model=cfg.model_planner, api_key=cfg.openai_api_key, user_msg=state["user_msg"])
    state["plan"] = decision
    if decision.refusal:
        state["refusal"] = True
        state["refusal_reason"] = decision.unsafe_reason or "unsafe request"
    return state

def python_node(state: TurnState, cfg) -> TurnState:
    dec = state["plan"]
    if dec.use_python and python_expression_is_eligible(dec.python_expression):
        tool = run_safe_python(dec.python_expression or "")
        if tool.get("ok"):
            state["python_tool_result"] = tool["result"]
        else:
            state["python_tool_result"] = f"(python tool declined: {tool.get('error','error')})"
    return state

def retrieval_node(state: TurnState, cfg) -> TurnState:
    dec = state["plan"]
    if dec.need_retrieval:
        query = dec.retrieval_query or state["user_msg"]
        # your existing retriever call here -> results, citations
        results, citations = cfg.retriever.search(query)  # pseudo; adapt
        state["retrieval_results"] = results
        state["citations"] = citations
    return state

def answer_node(state: TurnState, cfg) -> TurnState:
    if state.get("refusal"):
        state["answer"] = f"Lo siento, no puedo ayudar con eso: {state.get('refusal_reason','')}".strip()
        return state
    # Compose a grounded answer; include python_tool_result if present, and cite if required
    dec = state["plan"]
    answer = cfg.answer_synthesizer.compose(
        user_msg=state["user_msg"],
        python_result=state.get("python_tool_result"),
        passages=state.get("retrieval_results") or [],
        require_citations=dec.answer_requires_citations,
        citations=state.get("citations") or [],
    )
    state["answer"] = answer
    return state

def build_graph(cfg):
    g = StateGraph(TurnState)
    g.add_node("planner", lambda s: planner_node(s, cfg))
    g.add_node("python",  lambda s: python_node(s, cfg))
    g.add_node("retrieve",lambda s: retrieval_node(s, cfg))
    g.add_node("answer",  lambda s: answer_node(s, cfg))

    # entry
    g.set_entry_point("planner")

    # conditional branches driven by the plan
    def go_python(s: TurnState):   return s["plan"].use_python and not s.get("refusal", False)
    def go_retrieve(s: TurnState): return s["plan"].need_retrieval and not s.get("refusal", False)

    g.add_conditional_edges("planner", {
        go_python: "python",
        (lambda s: not go_python(s) and go_retrieve(s)): "retrieve",
        (lambda s: s.get("refusal", False)): "answer",
    }, default="answer")

    # If Python ran, continue to retrieval if needed; else go answer
    g.add_conditional_edges("python", {
        go_retrieve: "retrieve",
    }, default="answer")

    # After retrieval, always answer
    g.add_edge("retrieve", "answer")
    g.add_edge("answer", END)
    return g.compile()

How the turn flows now

  1. Planner LLM returns a JSON plan (no reasoning leakage).

  2. Double-gate: if use_python=true, we still check python_expression_is_eligible(expr).

  3. If eligible, we call Safe Python Tool; if not, we skip and continue.

  4. If need_retrieval=true, we run the retriever.

  5. Answer node composes the final response, including the Python result and citations when requested by the plan.

Notes & small tips

  • Keep the planner model small and cheap (0 temperature). It’s pattern classification, not generation.

  • You can bias the planner with quick keywords (e.g., if digits + “convert/calculate/regex” → encourage use_python=true) by adding one line of instruction in PLANNER_SYSTEM, but let the LLM make the final call.

  • The no-CoT JSON instruction avoids returning internal reasoning; the plan is all we need.

If you’re happy, I can next wire the answer_synthesizer.compose(...) helper (so it nicely merges Python results + retrieved snippets + citations), or jump straight to the image caption ingestion module.

Below I show (1) why this change is safe and useful, and (2) a surgical patch to your graph.py that adds an LLM Planner node and optional Python Tool execution.

Why do this?

  • Smarter branching. The LLM plans per-turn: “compute first” (use Python), “retrieve sources”, or both.

  • Still safe. We keep your guard as the very first node. Before calling the Python Tool, we run a tiny eligibility check (and your tool is already sandboxed).

  • Minimal disruption. You keep the same retriever, memory, prompt style, and CLI. Just add a planner and one more (optional) node.

5) LLM Planner + tiny Python eligibility check – ADD

python
# -------------------------
# Planner (LLM) + Python eligibility
# -------------------------
PLANNER_SYSTEM = """You are a planner for a RAG+Tools assistant.
Decide for each user message whether to:
- use_python: for SMALL, deterministic computations (arithmetic, unit conversion, tiny list stats).
- need_retrieval: fetch knowledge from the indexed PDFs (text + image captions).
- refusal: true only if unsafe/out-of-scope.

Strict constraints:
- If use_python=true, python_expression MUST be a SINGLE pure expression using only: + - * / // % (), lists/tuples/dicts,
  and functions: len, sum, min, max, sorted, round, abs.
- NO imports, NO attribute access, NO comprehensions, NO assignments, NO dunders.
- If need_retrieval=true, provide a concise retrieval_query.
Return JSON ONLY.
"""

def plan_with_llm(cfg: RagConfig, user_msg: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
    llm = ChatOpenAI(model=cfg.planner_model, api_key=cfg.openai_api_key, temperature=0)
    prompt_txt = (
        f"{PLANNER_SYSTEM}\n\nUser message:\n{user_msg}\n\n"
        "Respond with JSON keys: refusal, unsafe_reason, use_python, python_expression, "
        "need_retrieval, retrieval_query, answer_requires_citations, confidence.\n"
    )
    raw = llm.invoke([{"role": "system", "content": PLANNER_SYSTEM},
                      {"role": "user", "content": prompt_txt}]).content
    try:
        return json.loads(raw)
    except Exception:
        # Fallback: retrieval by default
        return {
            "refusal": False,
            "unsafe_reason": None,
            "use_python": False,
            "python_expression": None,
            "need_retrieval": True,
            "retrieval_query": None,
            "answer_requires_citations": True,
            "confidence": 0.5,
        }

BLOCK_SUBSTRINGS = ["__", "import", "open(", "exec(", "eval(", "os.", "sys.", "subprocess", "class", "lambda", " for ", " while "]
ALLOWED_FUNC_TOKENS = ("len(", "sum(", "min(", "max(", "sorted(", "round(", "abs(")

def python_expression_is_eligible(expr: Optional[str]) -> bool:
    if not expr:
        return False
    s = expr.strip().lower()
    if any(b in s for b in BLOCK_SUBSTRINGS):
        return False
    has_ops = any(ch in s for ch in "()*/+-%,[]{}")
    has_allowed_fn = s.startswith(ALLOWED_FUNC_TOKENS) or any(f in s for f in ALLOWED_FUNC_TOKENS)
    has_digit = any(ch.isdigit() for ch in s)
    return has_ops or has_allowed_fn or has_digit

6) New nodes – ADD

Add planner and python nodes alongside your existing nodes:

python
def make_planner_node(cfg: RagConfig):
    def planner(state: RAGState) -> RAGState:
        decision = plan_with_llm(cfg, state["question"])
        state["plan"] = decision
        # Honor your guard first; planner can also suggest refusal but guard is authoritative
        if decision.get("refusal"):
            return {
                "answer": "Lo siento, no puedo ayudar con esa solicitud.",
                "docs": [],
            }
        return {"plan": decision}
    return planner

def make_python_node():
    def python_exec(state: RAGState) -> RAGState:
        plan = state.get("plan") or {}
        expr = plan.get("python_expression")
        if plan.get("use_python") and python_expression_is_eligible(expr):
            tool = run_safe_python(expr)
            if tool.get("ok"):
                return {"python_tool_result": tool["result"]}
            else:
                # Surface a gentle note, but don't fail the turn
                return {"python_tool_result": f"(python declined: {tool.get('error','error')})"}
        return {}
    return python_exec

def make_retrieve_node(retriever):
    def retrieve(state: RAGState) -> RAGState:
        plan = state.get("plan") or {}
        query = plan.get("retrieval_query") or state["question"]
        docs = retriever.get_relevant_documents(query)

Tweak the generate node to work even when there are no docs but there is a Python result:

python
def make_generate_node(cfg: RagConfig):
    llm = ChatOpenAI(
        model=cfg.chat_model,
        api_key=cfg.openai_api_key,
        temperature=cfg.temperature,
        max_tokens=cfg.max_tokens,
    )
    def generate(state: RAGState) -> RAGState:
        docs = state.get("docs", [])
        python_result = state.get("python_tool_result", "") or "(none)"
        # If planner chose no retrieval and we have a Python result, answer directly.
        plan = state.get("plan") or {}
        if (not docs) and plan.get("need_retrieval") is False and python_result and python_result != "(none)":
            return {"answer": f"Resultado del cálculo: {python_result}"}

        if not docs:
            return {"answer": state.get("answer") or "I couldn't find relevant passages in the indexed documents to answer that."}

        context_blocks, sources_list = build_context_blocks(docs)
        conv_summary = state.get("summary", "") or "(none)"
        recent_turns = render_recent_turns(state.get("history", []), last_pairs=cfg.memory_last_turns)

        messages = prompt.format_messages(
            conv_summary=conv_summary,
            recent_turns=recent_turns,
            python_tool_result=python_result,
            question=state["question"],
            context_blocks=context_blocks,
            sources_list=sources_list,
        )
        result = llm.invoke(messages)
        return {"answer": result.content}
    return generate

8) Graph wiring – CHANGE

Replace your current build_graph with this one (keeps guard first):

python
def build_graph(cfg: RagConfig):
    retriever = get_retriever(cfg)

    graph = StateGraph(RAGState)
    graph.add_node("guard", make_guard_node())
    graph.add_node("planner", make_planner_node(cfg))
    graph.add_node("python", make_python_node())
    graph.add_node("retrieve", make_retrieve_node(retriever))
    graph.add_node("generate", make_generate_node(cfg))
    graph.add_node("mem_update", make_memory_node(cfg))
    graph.set_entry_point("guard")

    # After guard: blocked -> END, ok -> planner
    def _route_after_guard(state: RAGState) -> str:
        return "block" if state.get("blocked") else "ok"
    graph.add_conditional_edges("guard", _route_after_guard, {"block": END, "ok": "planner"})

    # After planner:
    def _use_python(state: RAGState) -> bool:
        p = state.get("plan") or {}
        return bool(p.get("use_python"))

    def _need_retrieval(state: RAGState) -> bool:
        p = state.get("plan") or {}
        return bool(p.get("need_retrieval"))

    graph.add_conditional_edges("planner", {
        _use_python: "python",
        _need_retrieval: "retrieve",
    }, default="generate")

    # If Python ran, optionally retrieve; else go generate
    graph.add_conditional_edges("python", {
        _need_retrieval: "retrieve",
    }, default="generate")

    graph.add_edge("retrieve", "generate")
    graph.add_edge("generate", "mem_update")
    graph.add_edge("mem_update", END)

    return graph.compile()

  • Compute-only:

  • Both:
    --query "Según el documento, ¿cuánto es 10% de 250 y en qué página se menciona el IVA?" → Python runs, then retrieval, and the answer includes sources while using the computed number.

        # Capture messages so tests can assert that PYTHON TOOL RESULT is included

def test_python_expression_not_eligible(monkeypatch):
    """
    Planner suggests a malicious expression; eligibility guard should prevent calling the tool.
    Since need_retrieval=False and no docs, we fall back to the 'not found' message.
    """

        graph, "plan_with_llm",
        lambda cfg, user_msg: {
            "refusal": False,
            "unsafe_reason": None,
            "use_python": True,
            "python_expression": "__import__('os').system('ls')",
            "need_retrieval": False,
            "retrieval_query": None,
            "answer_requires_citations": False,
            "confidence": 0.99,
        }
    )

    # Ensure run_safe_python is NOT called (would fail test if it is)
    def _should_not_run(_expr):
        raise AssertionError("run_safe_python should not be called for ineligible expressions")
    monkeypatch.setattr(graph, "run_safe_python", _should_not_run)

    monkeypatch.setattr(graph, "get_retriever", lambda cfg: FakeRetriever(docs=[]))
    monkeypatch.setattr(graph, "ChatOpenAI", FakeLLM)

    app = graph.build_graph(make_cfg())
    out = app.invoke({"question": " do malicious "})
    assert "couldn't find relevant passages" in out["answer"].lower()

Good catch — this is a typing/annotations issue.

Why it fails:
StateGraph inspects your RAGState with typing.get_type_hints. Because you have from __future__ import annotations, your annotations are stored as strings and then evaluated. Since Optional wasn’t imported into the module’s globals, get_type_hints can’t resolve it → NameError: 'Optional' is not defined.

Fix (choose one)

Option A — Import Optional (simplest)

Add Optional to your typing imports at the top of src/rag/graph.py.

python
# existing
from typing import List, TypedDict, Dict, Any
# change to
from typing import List, TypedDict, Dict, Any, Optional

(You already added an Optional[str] field: python_tool_result: Optional[str]. This makes it resolvable.)

Option B — Use PEP 604 unions (Py 3.11+)

If you prefer modern syntax and want to avoid Optional entirely, change the field to:

python
class RAGState(TypedDict, total=False):
    # ...
    python_tool_result: str | None

Either approach is fine; Option A is the quickest.
